label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-Tp — The sink expression at L59-L62 writes encoded SQL to the response, but the resolved sink value is the raw SQL string containing user input because ESAPI.encoder().encodeForHTML(sql) encodes the entire SQL string including the injected payload, making the XSS vulnerable. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): alert-Tp — The resolved sink value for sql at L56 is constructed as "SELECT..." + bar, where bar comes from the user-supplied header via doSomething(), allowing direct SQL injection. Both alerts represent real vulnerabilities.

evidence.note: User input flows from request header -> param -> decoded param -> doSomething -> bar -> sql construction.
doSomething method resolves bar to valuesList.get(1) which is the user-provided param after removing the first safe element.
SQL injection sink at L56 uses raw bar in query execution; XSS sink at L59-L62 writes encoded SQL to response but the encoding happens after concatenation so payload remains executable in DB context.
